x: Much to everyone's surprise the Handicapper gave him 2 mins. start and Dan certainly made the best use of it. There was a tie for second place, this being between H.
Then came Tom Carter, Les Cohen and Harry Verney, of the "Bels"; followed by L. Scott, of Mitcham, with that old war-horse Bert Footer next.
Harry Verney, who was expected to run in the Middlesex team, was forced to stand down owing to a knee injury received in France the previous week.

Harry Verney had also run a good race and was just beaten by an old team mate in Kibble, of Birchfield. Our third man was Syd Ring, who was quite a fair way back, but when they had totalled up the points the result was: Belgrave H. 33, Surrey A.C.35, Highgate H. 38

…eed that but for our bad luck on the second stage, and seeing the way our lads ran on the subsequent stages (especially Harry Verney on the third and Pat Parker over the final leg), given ordinary luck this time we shall be right there.…
The Club gratefully acknowledges vests from Bill Luther (Erith), Cyril Pateman (Ceylon and S.W.19), H.
Harry Verney was soon found a job when he visited us, and he looked as if he was enjoying the sound of shoes on mud again. Syd Warboys has moved from Essex to Wallasey, Cheshire.

In our team for the first time were Len Herbert, due to become an International later, Harry Verney and Charlie Smart. Mitcham's hat-trick of wins was recorded in 1939 when we were second and Birchfield third.
7th A.W.Penny,9th J.Parker,11th H.E.Footer, 23rd C.T.Carter, 27th L.J.Cohen 32nd R.W.Tobin, 34th D.Patience, 117th H.G.
